items.title: 11.4.2 Graph of y = sin x from - 2pi to 2pi (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 206-207: 11.4.2 Graph of y = sin x: range lines y = +/-1, table x / sin x, 'To draw the graph' steps (i)-(iv), Note box, graphs 0 to 360 and -360 to 360, 'cycle', properties (i)-(xi).

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum apna pehla asal trigonometric graph banayenge: \(y = \sin x\). Yeh graph ek lehar (wave) jaisa hota hai, bilkul samandar ki lehron ya jhoole ki tarah jo upar jata hai, neeche aata hai, aur yahi harkat baar baar dohrata hai. Physics mein sound waves aur alternating current bhi isi shakal ki hoti hain, is liye yeh graph aage bohat kaam aayega.
Kitab pehle yaad dilati hai ke sine function ka period \(2\pi\) hai, is liye hum pehle graph sirf \(0^{\circ}\) se \(360^{\circ}\) (yani \(0\) se \(2\pi\)) tak banayenge.

Graph se pehle yeh yaad rakhiye ke har real \(x\) ke liye \(-1 \le \sin x \le 1\). Sine function ki range \([-1, 1]\) hai, is liye graph horizontal lines \(y = +1\) aur \(y = -1\) ke darmiyan hi rahega.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh do baatein humara kaam bohat chhota kar deti hain:
Period \(2\pi\) (dohrane ka waqfa): \(360^{\circ}\) ke baad values wapas wahi aa jati hain. Jaise ghari ki sui 12 ghante baad wapas wahin hoti hai. Is liye sirf ek hissa (\(0\) se \(2\pi\)) bana lein, baaqi graph usi ki copy hai.
Range \([-1, 1]\): curve kabhi \(y = 1\) se upar ya \(y = -1\) se neeche nahin jata. Is liye pehle yeh do lines dashed (tooti hui) bana lein; yeh graph ke liye frame ka kaam karti hain.
\(y = \sin x\) ko satisfy karne wale ordered pairs ki table yeh hai:

blocks.caption: Ordered pairs satisfying \(y = \sin x\), \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\) (printed across the page in the book; turned on its side here to fit a phone)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh values kahan se aayin? \(\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5\) aur \(\sin 60^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.87\) hum jaante hain. Baaqi 11.4 ki identities se: \(\sin 150^{\circ} = \sin(180^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}) = 0.5\), aur \(\sin 240^{\circ} = \sin(180^{\circ} + 60^{\circ}) = -\sin 60^{\circ} = -0.87\).
Ek khoobsurat pattern dekhiye: \(180^{\circ}\) se \(360^{\circ}\) tak ki values bilkul wahi hain jo \(0^{\circ}\) se \(180^{\circ}\) tak thin, bas minus ke saath. Kyun? Kyun ke \(\sin(\pi + \theta) = -\sin\theta\). Yani graph ka doosra hissa pehle hisse ka ulta (upside down) roop hai.
To draw the graph:

items: (i) Munasib scale lijiye: \(x\)-axis par graph paper ke chhote khane ki ek side \(= 10^{\circ}\); \(y\)-axis par bare khane ki ek side \(= 1\) unit.
(iii) Upar wali table ke ordered pairs ke points plot kijiye, yani \((0, 0)\), \((30^{\circ}, 0.5)\), \((60^{\circ}, 0.87)\) waghaira.
(iv) Points ko ek smooth curve se joriye, jaisa figure mein dikhaya gaya hai. Is tarah humein \(y = \sin x\) ka graph \(0\) se \(360^{\circ}\), yani \(0\) se \(2\pi\) tak mil jata hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Scale ka matlab: graph paper ka har chhota khana \(x\)-axis par \(10^{\circ}\) ke barabar, yani \(30^{\circ}\) ke liye teen chhote khane. \(y\)-axis par ek bara khana \(1\) unit. \(0.87\) jaisi value ke liye bare khane ko andaze se nahin, balke chhote khanon se naap kar point lagaiye.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Trigonometric functions ke graphs smooth curves hote hain: in mein koi bhi line segments se bana hua nahin, aur apne domain ke andar kisi mein nukeela kona ya toot nahin hoti. Curve ke is rawaiye ko continuity kehte hain; matlab trigonometric functions jahan bhi defined hain wahan continuous hain. Mazeed yeh ke trigonometric functions periodic hain, is liye un ke curves ek muqarrar waqfe ke baad dohraye jate hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab ka Note samajhiye: 'continuity' (tasalsul) ka matlab hai ke graph mein koi jhatka, koi toot ya nukeela kona nahin. Aap pencil uthaye baghair poora curve bana sakte hain. Aur periodic hone ka matlab: ek tukra baar baar dohraya jata hai, jaise deewar par ek hi design wale tiles.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = sin x from 0 to 360 degrees. The x-axis is marked every 30 degrees (with pi/2, pi, 3pi/2, 2pi below), the y-axis at 1, 0.5, -0.5, -1, and dashed lines y = 1 and y = -1. The 13 table points are plotted and joined by one smooth wave: it starts at (0, 0), rises to the maximum (90, 1), comes down through (180, 0) to the minimum (270, -1) and returns to (360, 0).
blocks.caption: Graph of y = sin x from 0° to 360° (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab is graph ko chaar hisson mein parhiye:
\(0^{\circ}\) se \(90^{\circ}\): curve \(0\) se barh kar \(1\) tak jata hai (sab se ooncha point).
\(90^{\circ}\) se \(180^{\circ}\): wapas \(0\) par aa jata hai.
\(180^{\circ}\) se \(270^{\circ}\): neeche \(-1\) tak chala jata hai (sab se neecha point).
\(270^{\circ}\) se \(360^{\circ}\): wapas \(0\) par.
Ghor kijiye: Quadrant I aur II mein curve \(x\)-axis ke upar (positive) hai, III aur IV mein neeche (negative). Yeh bilkul wahi sign hain jo sine ke quadrants mein hote hain. Graph aur quadrant wala rule ek doosre ki tasdeeq karte hain.

Isi tarah hum \(0^{\circ}\) se \(-360^{\circ}\) tak ka graph bhi bana sakte hain. Is se \(y = \sin x\) ka graph \(-360^{\circ}\) se \(360^{\circ}\) (yani \(-2\pi\) se \(2\pi\)) tak mukammal ho jata hai, jo neeche diya gaya hai:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Negative angles ki values ke liye \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\) istemal kijiye: \(\sin(-30^{\circ}) = -0.5\), \(\sin(-90^{\circ}) = -1\), \(\sin(-270^{\circ}) = 1\). Yani bayen (left) taraf ka graph, dayen taraf wale graph ko origin ke gird aadha chakkar (\(180^{\circ}\)) ghuma kar mil jata hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = sin x from -360 to 360 degrees (-2pi to 2pi), x-axis marked every 90 degrees with radian names, points every 30 degrees. Two complete waves between the dashed lines y = 1 and y = -1: maxima at -270 and 90 degrees, minima at -90 and 270 degrees, zeros at -360, -180, 0, 180, 360 degrees. The curve passes through the origin.
blocks.caption: Graph of y = sin x from −360° to 360° (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Interval \([0, 2\pi]\) wale graph ko ek cycle (chakkar) kehte hain. Chunke sine function ka period \(2\pi\) hai, is liye sine ka graph \(x\)-axis ki dono taraf har \(2\pi\) ke interval mein aage barhaya ja sakta hai.
Properties of graph of sine function (y = sin x)
Ab kitab graph ki gyarah (11) properties batati hai. Har property ko graph par ungli rakh kar check kijiye; is tarah yeh ratne ki zaroorat nahin parti:

items: (i) Domain tamam real numbers ka set hai \((-\infty < x < \infty)\): har angle ka sine maujood hai, koi angle mana nahin.
(ii) Range mein \(-1\) se \(1\) tak ke tamam real numbers shamil hain, dono kinare bhi: \([-1, 1]\).
(iii) Sine ka graph tamam real numbers par continuous hai, yani kahin bhi toot-ta nahin.
(iv) Sine function ka period \(2\pi\) hai. Formula ki zubaan mein: \(\sin(\theta + 2\pi) = \sin\theta\).
(v) Sine odd function hai, kyun ke us ka graph origin ke gird symmetric hai. Formula: \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\).
(vi) \(y = \sin x\) ki maximum (sab se bari) value \(1\) hai, jab \(x = \frac{\pi}{2} + 2\pi n\), jahan \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\) (koi bhi integer).
(vii) \(y = \sin x\) ki minimum (sab se chhoti) value \(-1\) hai, jab \(x = \frac{3\pi}{2} + 2\pi n\), jahan \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
(viii) Sine ka \(x\)-intercept (jahan graph \(x\)-axis ko kaatta hai) \(x = \pi n\) par hota hai, jahan \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
(ix) Sine ka \(y\)-intercept \(0\) hai: graph \(y\)-axis ko origin par kaatta hai.
(x) Sine function ka amplitude (lehar ki unchai) \(1\) hai.
(xi) Unit circle mein \(\sin\theta\) diye gaye point ke \(y\)-coordinate ke barabar hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Properties ko graph par yun milaiye:
(vi) mein \(n = 0\) rakhein to \(x = 90^{\circ}\), aur \(n = -1\) rakhein to \(x = -270^{\circ}\). Figure mein dono jagah choti (peak) hai.
(viii) mein \(n = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2\) se \(-360^{\circ}, -180^{\circ}, 0^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}, 360^{\circ}\) milte hain: bilkul wahi jagah jahan curve \(x\)-axis ko kaatta hai.
(x) amplitude (lehar ki unchai) \(1\) hai: yani \(x\)-axis se choti tak ki unchai.
(xi) unit circle par point \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) hota hai; sine us point ki unchai (\(y\)-coordinate) hai. Point circle par ghoomta hai to uski unchai upar neeche hoti hai: yahi lehar graph mein nazar aati hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Practice ke liye (kitab ka sawal nahin): \(0^{\circ}\) se \(360^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan kin angles par \(\sin x = 0.5\) hai? Graph par \(y = 0.5\) ki horizontal line khenchiye; yeh lehar ko do jagah kaatti hai. Table se: \(30^{\circ}\) aur \(150^{\circ}\). Doosra jawab identity se bhi milta hai: \(\sin(180^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}) = \sin 30^{\circ}\). Jawab: \(x = 30^{\circ}\) aur \(x = 150^{\circ}\); dono Quadrant I aur II mein hain, jahan sine positive hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(y = \sin x\) ka graph \(x = 450^{\circ}\) par kitna ooncha hoga? Sochiye: \(450^{\circ} = 90^{\circ} + 360^{\circ}\), aur period \(360^{\circ}\) hai, to \(\sin 450^{\circ} = \sin 90^{\circ} = 1\). Property (vi) mein \(n = 1\) bhi yahi deta hai: \(\frac{\pi}{2} + 2\pi = \frac{5\pi}{2}\), yani \(450^{\circ}\).

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Maximum ya minimum poocha jaye to value ke saath yeh bhi likhiye ke kahan hota hai: maximum \(1\), jab \(x = \frac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\); minimum \(-1\), jab \(x = \frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Sirf 'maximum 1' likhne par poore marks nahin milte.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Table se ek cycle (\(0\) se \(2\pi\)) banaiye, phir har \(2\pi\) baad dohraiye.
2. Curve \(y = -1\) aur \(y = 1\) ke darmiyan rehta hai aur origin se guzarta hai.
3. Zeros \(n\pi\) par, chotiyan \(\frac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\) par, sab se neeche points \(\frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\) par.
4. Sine odd function hai: graph origin ke gird symmetric hai.
5. Graph smooth aur continuous lehar hai: na kona, na toot.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(90^{\circ}\) aur \(270^{\circ}\) par nukeeli chotiyan bana dena. Lehar ka ooper aur neeche wala hissa gol hota hai, jaise pahari ki gol choti.
2. Sine graph ko \((0, 1)\) se shuru karna: woh cosine hai. Sine hamesha origin \((0, 0)\) se shuru hota hai, kyun ke \(\sin 0 = 0\).
3. Period \(\pi\) likh dena. Ek poori lehar (upar bhi, neeche bhi) \(2\pi\) mein mukammal hoti hai.
4. Negative values (\(-0.5\), \(-0.87\)) ko \(x\)-axis ke upar laga dena: minus wali values hamesha axis ke neeche.
